title: RevBoost is now SubScale
author: John-Marcus Phillips
excerpt: Discover why RevBoost rebranded to SubScale and how its new operating system empowers subscription brands with smarter growth, automation, and long-term success.

toc.text: WHY THE NAME HAD TO GO

contentHtml:
This is the first thing we've published under the new name, so it’s a great opportunity explain how we arrived here.

I acquired RevBoost in 2025 because of something I saw in the way it made money.

Alex, original founder of RevBoost, had built the company in 2021 on a premise that sounds obvious now but was still emerging at the time: the money in e-commerce isn't in the first sale. It's in everything after it. The upsell. The rebill. The retention curve. The dozens of small improvements to an offer or a checkout that compound month over month until the unit economics finally work.

Most of the market was pointed at the front end i.e. more traffic, better creative, cheaper clicks. However RevBoost has always pointed at the part of the business that actually determines whether a subscription brand survives.

What I found under the hood wasn't just an agency. It was a system. A specific sequence of things you do to a subscription business, in a specific order, that reliably moves LTV, approval rates, retention, and cash flow — including the compliance work that keeps a processor from shutting the whole thing down on a Tuesday.

That system is THE asset. The name just described the system.

WHY THE NAME HAD TO GO

"Boost" is a word for a moment. You boost a number, it goes up, and you go find another number to boost.

But that wasn’t what our partners were buying. Nobody signs a multi-year partnership for a moment. They sign because they wanted the machine underneath their revenue to work permanently, predictably, without thinking about it every morning. Our longest-running partner is five years in and still scaling. You don't get five years out of a boost.

SubScale is the name for what the work already was: subscription brands, scaling with structure.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES

The RevBoost system works, and it runs on expertise, hard work, and people paying very close attention. That scales to a point and then it doesn't.

So we are building the infrastructure underneath it. Same decisions the system always made — now instrumented, measured, and increasingly automated. We will share more as the product rolls out, but a couple of highlights worth calling out:

One source of truth for revenue. Most merchants can't answer "what is a customer from this channel actually worth at 90 days" without three exports and a lost afternoon. Every good decision downstream depends on fixing that first.

Decisions that run themselves. Cohort LTV forecasting so you know which channels are genuinely profitable. Cross-processor routing that protects authorization rates. Failed payments recovered and churn caught before the charge fails, not after the cancel click.

Readiness for agentic commerce. AI agents are starting to discover products, compare offers, and transact for consumers. They may care less about optimized funnels or fixed subscription schedules, but recurring demand won’t disappear. VIP relationships can give customers and their agents a reason to keep choosing the same merchant.

SAME SKIN IN THE GAME

One thing carries over unchanged: we only get paid when a partner's subscription revenue grows. It's the only arrangement that keeps both sides honest about whether the work is working.

RevBoost proved the thesis: subscription growth is a systems problem, not just a traffic problem.

RevBoost was the origin. SubScale is the operating system for what comes next.
